chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, said:

I wrote to Abu Muhammad عليه السلام asking him: May one perform salat (prayer) in a cap upon which there is the fur of that whose flesh is not eaten, or in a belt of pure silk, or in a belt made from the fur of rabbits? So he wrote: Salat (prayer) is not lawful in pure silk. But if the fur is from a duly slaughtered animal, salat (prayer) in it is lawful, if Allah wills.

key_terms.تِكَّةِ: a waistband, cord, or belt-like garment accessory
key_terms.ذَكِيًّا: from an animal properly slaughtered according to the law
key_terms.قَلَنْسُوَةٍ: a cap or head-covering worn in salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: an animal whose flesh is not lawful to eat
key_terms.وَبَرُ: fur or fine hair attached to or made into clothing

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in pure silk or in clothing made from rabbit fur according to Imam Abu Muhammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) in garments made of pure silk and items containing animal fur. It states that salat (prayer) in pure silk is not permitted, while salat (prayer) in fur is permitted if the fur is from an animal that is dhakiyy.
